name: Tournament day
summary: Teams playing through rounds on a handful of pitches in a single day, with officials to spread across the matches and a break in the middle.
when_to_choose: Choose this if you are running a one-day competition rather than a weekly timetable: every team plays several matches, no team plays twice at once, and the day has to finish on time.

knobs.label: Days the tournament runs
knobs.help: One for a single day. Two or three for a weekend competition.

knobs.label: Teams entered
knobs.help: How many teams are playing in total, across all groups.

knobs.label: Rounds to play
knobs.help: How many matches each team plays. Seven rounds lets eight teams each play everyone else once.

knobs.label: Pitches or courts
knobs.help: How many matches can be played at the same time.

questions: How many teams are entered, and do they play everyone else or only their group?
How many pitches or courts can run at once?
How long is a match, including the changeover before the next one?
What time does the first match start and what time must the last one finish?
How many officials do you have, and does each match need more than one?
tradeoffs: More pitches finish the day sooner, but each one needs its own official, and a tournament usually runs out of officials before it runs out of grass.
Every team playing everyone else is the fairest result, but it grows fast: doubling the teams roughly quadruples the matches, and at some point the day is longer than the teams can play.

Back-to-back matches keep teams warm and the day short, but a team that plays three in a row is at a real disadvantage in the third; a guaranteed round off between matches costs an hour and is the single fairest thing you can do.
